reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that event-based data in soccer lacks continuous temporal resolution, making direct velocity calculation impossible. The proposed method addresses this by treating velocity completion as a structured inference problem over a graph-temporal framework. Each event provides a snapshot of positions, but velocity must be reconstructed using prior knowledge of motion dynamics and inter-agent relationships. A neural network is trained to map event-based positional inputs to velocity outputs, leveraging both spatial proximity (via graph structure) and temporal consistency (via recurrent layers). The model assumes smooth motion and local interaction dominance, enabling accurate imputation even under sparse sampling. Failure occurs when events are too infrequent or when global motion patterns override local dynamics. The method bridges discrete event data with continuous motion models, enabling downstream analytics like space evaluation that require velocity.
